# Mobiles — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Mobile Phones: typically around Rs 20,000, most listings Rs 5,000-75,000 (124 listings).
- Mobile Phone Accessories: typically around Rs 1,400, most listings Rs 600-16,000 (54 listings).
- Wearables: typically around Rs 1,500, most listings Rs 450-15,000 (10 listings — thin data, lean on general judgment).

Phones are high-value goods: a recognizable model priced far below its market range (e.g. a current-gen iPhone/Galaxy flagship at a fraction of typical resale) is a scam signal -> hold. Old/budget handsets legitimately sell for Rs 4,000-10,000, so low price alone on an old model is fine.

## What good listings look like
- "Iphone 17 256 GB Brand new" — Rs 142,000
- "Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra 12/256 GB Brand New" — Rs 159,999
- "iphone 8 128 gb" — Rs 15,000
- "8gb gaming phone huawei nova 7i" — Rs 10,500
- "iQOO 7 5G" — Rs 26,000

A typical good listing names brand + model, usually storage/RAM, and condition (brand new vs used); price matches the model's age. Casual lowercase/typos are normal here and not a problem.

## Category-specific hold signals
- Flagship or recent-model phone priced drastically below market for that model (classic too-good-to-be-true scam; editors have rejected "fake" listings here).
- "Brand new / sealed" claims at prices far below official Nepal retail for that model — suggests clone or misrepresented refurb.
- Obvious wrong-category items posted under Mobiles (real examples: a blanket, men's clothing) — hold for recategorization; ignore genuine phone accessories/wearables, which belong here.
